title: A Wolf for the Garden
premise: Silas Blackwood, a memory-thief and reluctant bookkeeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent a lifetime staying unrecorded—until prayers to the old gods start being answered with fire. When a dying priest presses a stolen prayer into Silas's hands, they discover the god answering is not a god at all but a bound king, hollowed out by the thing that wears his crown. To free him, Silas must gather a found family of guild misfits, trade away their most precious memories as payment, and walk into the usurper's capital as the armies march on the free cities. In the end, Silas gives up their own name—every memory of who they were—to unbind the king, saving the cities at the cost of ever knowing why the people who love them weep when they smile.
about_author: Quentin Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries that no longer exist. They write fantasy about people who survive by keeping accounts, and live somewhere with too many doors.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Silas Blackwood audits the Guild of Impossible Things' ledgers by candlelight, trading in bottled memories and impossible favors while keeping their own past deliberately blank. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: wary contentment—the comfort of a life built on not being known.

chapters.title: A Prayer, Answered
chapters.summary: A dying priest stumbles into the guildhouse clutching a prayer that was answered—and burns the messenger who delivered it. Silas reads the prayer aloud and hears something ancient stir in reply. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread; the first crack in Silas's invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Gods Charge
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Odessa Vane reveals the old gods are answering prayers again across the free cities, each miracle leaving a worshipper hollowed. She orders Silas to trace the pattern through debt-records only they can read. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: reluctant duty overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Sold His Birthday
chapters.summary: Following the ledger trail, Silas finds Tam, a child who sold his happiest memory to a shrine and now cannot remember his mother's face. His memory bottle hums with the same resonance as the prayer. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: fierce protectiveness—the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Shrine Road
chapters.summary: Silas and Tam travel to a roadside shrine where an entire village prayed for rain and received it—at the price of every villager's name. The rain still falls, black and warm. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Kept Accounts
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how young Silas learned to steal memories from a cruel master and erased their own childhood to escape him. POV: Silas (past). Emotional beat: grief for a self they chose to lose.

chapters.title: An Army on the Horizon
chapters.summary: News reaches the free cities: the usurper King Aldric's armies march, and his priests promise miracles to any city that surrenders. One refusing city is already ash. POV: alternating Silas and Odessa. Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Lost Things
chapters.summary: Silas recruits Wren, a disgraced cartographer who maps places that have been erased from existence—including, she claims, a kingdom that vanished two hundred years ago: the true home of the bound king. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cautious alliance between liars.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Hollow
chapters.summary: In a drowned chapel, Silas trades memories to a hollowed worshipper for fragments of the truth: the 'god' answering prayers is a king, bound beneath his own crown, screaming through every miracle. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: pity curdling into anger.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Smile
chapters.summary: POV shift into the capital: King Aldric, wearing a crown that whispers, reviews conquest plans while small parts of himself go missing each day. He cannot remember his daughter's laugh. Emotional beat: dawning terror inside the villain.

chapters.title: Debts Called Due
chapters.summary: The guild's enemies use the chaos to raid the guildhouse; Odessa is gravely wounded defending the ledgers, and Silas must burn decades of records to save her life. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice—the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: What We Keep, What We Give
chapters.summary: Around Odessa's sickbed, the ragtag company—Silas, Tam, Wren, and the guild's one-eyed locksmith Brann—swear an oath to reach the capital before the armies do. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: found family solidifying into purpose.

chapters.title: The Road Through the Erased Kingdom
chapters.summary: Wren leads them along roads that exist only on her forbidden maps, through a kingdom unmade two centuries ago, where the bound king's loyal dead still keep watch. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by sorrow.

chapters.title: The Loyal Dead
chapters.summary: The dead knights test the travelers with riddles of loyalty; Tam offers his last happy memory freely, and the dead recognize the shape of a king's own sacrifice in it. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: a child's courage shaming adults into honesty.

chapters.title: Crown of Whispers
chapters.summary: The dead reveal the binding ritual: the crown was forged to cage the king's soul, and only a willing memory-sacrifice of equal weight can unbind him. Aldric's armies are three days behind them. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the trap of the price becoming clear.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Brann, secretly indebted to the usurper's spymaster, sells their route—but at the ford he sees what the crown did to Aldric's soldiers and turns his coat, buying the company time with his freedom. POV: Brann. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at capture.

chapters.title: Into the Capital
chapters.summary: Disguised as miracle-pilgrims, Silas, Tam, and Wren infiltrate the capital during a mass healing ceremony and witness the crown feeding on thousands at once. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: revulsion and vertigo beneath splendor.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Silas reaches Aldric's mind through a stolen memory and meets the bound king—a gentle, broken man who begs not for rescue but for someone to remember he existed. POV: Silas and Aldric interleaved. Emotional beat: compassion for the monster's prisoner.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: At the coronation anniversary rite, the company acts: Wren maps the ritual chamber, Tam carries the dead knights' token, and Silas begins pouring memories into the crown's hunger. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into offering.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: The crown demands a memory of equal weight to a soul: Silas surrenders every memory of themselves—their name, their thefts, their loves. The king tears free; the crown shatters; Aldric collapses, human again, as the armies halt mid-march. POV: Silas, fragmenting. Emotional beat: climax—self-annihilation as salvation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Miracles
chapters.summary: The free cities stand; the hollowed worshippers slowly regrow their names like scars. A nameless stranger wakes in the ruined guildhouse, kind hands reaching for them. POV: rotating—Wren, Tam, Odessa, Aldric. Emotional beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Garden
chapters.summary: Months later, the family tends a garden behind the rebuilt guildhouse, teaching the nameless Silas who they were through stories they can't feel but choose to believe. When asked if they want their memories back, Silas says some debts are better paid than reclaimed. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—identity rebuilt by love rather than recall.
